text:
ashley: Heads-up — since 07:12 UTC we see throughput drop on rack54 GPU pool, latency spikes on a few prod hosts. 10-20% request timeouts for long-generations.

mike: I was looking at metrics, nvlink retransmit rate jumped on node r54-n04 around 07:09. Also PCIe AER counts rising. link flaps every ~30s.

jia: can you paste the dmesg? guessing AER Xid 31/65 pattern.

ashley: dmesg snippet:
```
[07:09:12] pcieport 0000:01:00.0: AER: Multiple Uncorr Error
[07:09:12] nvlink0: link state change: DOWN -> UP
[07:09:12] NVRM: Xid (00000021): GPU has fallen off the bus
[07:09:42] pcieport 0000:01:00.0: AER: Multiple Uncorr Error
[07:09:42] nvlink0: link state change: DOWN -> UP
```

ivan: that Xid 0x21 matches ECC/unrecoverable GPU faults. Which GPU model? r54-n04 has A100-40GB on PCIe riser 2.

mike: confirmed `nvidia-smi -q -d ECC` shows rising single-bit and double-bit ECC on GPU2. ECC DBE count climbed by 13 in 10 minutes.

hardware-team: please hold on RMA until we try firmware/bios fallbacks. We saw similar on rack11 where a BIOS update toggled PCIe ASPM and made AER noise worse.

ashley: good call. I can repro locally by toggling ASPM from L1 to disabled. If we disable ASPM kernel param it reduces flaps. Want to try hotfix on one node.

jia: suggest steps: 1) drain r54-n04 from serving pool 2) apply kernel param `pcie_aspm=off` 3) reboot and monitor for 30m 4) if stable, replicate across rack54. Any objections? :thinking_face:

mike: agree. Also route traffic to us-west-2-dedicated for high-latency gen to avoid customer impact — capacity there has ~20% headroom.

ivan: make sure to annotate ticket and attach `dmesg` + `nvidia-smi` output. If ASPM off helps, we'll need vendor firmware follow-up. Could be flaky riser/cable causing NVLink retrains.

sre-bot: Auto-note: draining r54-n04 scheduled at 07:42 UTC by ashley. Will mark node DRAINING in cluster state.

ashley: Performing drain now: `kubectl cordon node=r54-n04 && kubectl drain r54-n04 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data` (reacted with :white_check_mark:)

ashley: Rebooted with `pcie_aspm=off` and collected post-reboot dmesg. so far 18m stable, no AER entries.

mike: Nice. Can you run a quick perf test against a few long-gen traces? I want to see token-per-second recovery.

ashley: perf runs show 12% throughput improvement vs baseline after change. Re-enabling NVLink retrain logs are gone.

hardware-team: Since this reduces failures, we'll schedule vendor RMA for riser on r54-n04 and open a firmware case. Also recommend we test ASPM toggles across 3 canaries before fleet wide.

jia: cost note — routing to dedicated added ~0.8% infra cost for the past hour; filing a short postmortem and cost delta in #incidents.

ivan: if canary is stable for 48h, we should roll change cluster-wide with runbook and rollback. Also add monitoring alert: AER-rate spike > 5/min -> auto-drain candidate.

mike: thanks team. I'll update on-call runbook and add the `dmesg` snippet to the incident doc. Closing loop once RMA confirmed.
__notes: Generated synthetic Slack thread for GPU/PCIe/NVLink triage. Follow agents.md: single-thread text with prefixed senders. No title field.
